Whatever is chosen must NOT silence genuine host OOMs.

title: P1 — bunker-mvp systemd-logind wedge is UNMONITORED: 46 bunkerd spawn failures in 24h (2026-10-14) produced zero alerts and zero board rows — only the mischief-chaos satellite's two SKIPped plane folds surfaced it
reasoning:
Found 2026-10-14 while triaging two consecutive mischief-chaos plane SKIPs (CHAOS-3, mischief board). Symptom on the fleet side: bunker-mvp answered `bunker list` with 4/50 agents, ssh up 12 days, / 61% used, 12G RAM available — yet every spawn died at stage rootless-install with "enable linger for bunker-<id>: Could not enable linger: Connection timed out".

LIVE EVIDENCE (measured this tick, ssh root@bunker-mvp):
- systemd-logind PID 24775 had been up 12 days, RSS 299MB, state R, holding 178 entries in /run/systemd/sessions.
- `busctl introspect org.freedesktop.login1 .../Manager` TIMED OUT (25s cap, empty output), while org.freedesktop.systemd1 and org.freedesktop.hostname1 on the SAME system bus both answered — so the wedge is logind-specific, not a dbus outage.
- `loginctl list-users` -> "Failed to list users: Connection timed out".
- bunkerd journal, 24h window: 46 "enable linger" failures; failing agent ids include 40306bbb, 59112a6a, eb84b8d4, 40d13b0d, 3860f968, b80b877b, 98823e1a, cc2e8a54, 5158ec82, ef382842. Per-hour failure line counts: Oct 14 02h=779, 03h=289, 04h=198, 05h=502.
- Remediation applied at 05:47Z: `systemctl restart systemd-logind` (Stopping 05:45:35, Started 05:47:05, new PID 2081843). After: 0 linger failures in the following 10+ minutes, logind RSS 299MB -> 26MB, and a plane run immediately PASSED (agent f27e5e74, TEARDOWN-GONE).

THE GAP: the monitoring stack has NO signal for this class. Nothing scrapes bunkerd's journal, nothing alerts on spawn-failure rate, nothing checks logind D-Bus liveness, and no exporter publishes agent counts or destroy-refused state. A host that is up, has disk, has RAM, and answers the bunker API can be completely unable to spawn agents for hours and the fleet sees nothing. It was discovered only because a chaos satellite's fold exit code went 3 twice.

ASK (stack work, belongs in /root/fleet-monitoring on fleet-monitor): (1) a bunkerd log-based alert — count of "enable linger"/"spawn agent failed"/"spawn failed" lines per host per 30m window > 0 for two consecutive windows = warning, > 5 = critical; (2) a logind liveness probe — `timeout 10 busctl introspect org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager` exit nonzero = critical (this catches the wedge ~hours before the spawn failures accumulate); (3) optionally an agent-state exporter publishing per-server agent count and destroy-refused count so the "4/50 but nothing spawns" contradiction is visible on a dashboard.

Cross-reference: mischief board CHAOS-3 (the two SKIPs this produced, now closed with the retry PASS) and MISCHIEF-DF-24 (bunker destroy refuses while any agent process is alive — same unreapable-agent family; three agents fa70ebf7/cb880c25/19d03bc5 still sit in destroy-refused:live_processes holding ~37.6G as of this tick).
resolution: FIXED 2026-10-14. Textfile exporter /usr/local/bin/bunker-health.sh on bunker-mvp (cron 2m) publishes bunker_logind_up + bunker_spawn_failures_30m via alloy textfile->remote_write. Prom rules BunkerLogindWedge (critical) + BunkerSpawnFailures (warning) in host-health.yml. Verified: gauge=1 at :9090, rules loaded. Commit 6e10538eb. Agent-state exporter (optional ask 3) deferred.

title: P0->ROOT-CAUSED — logind wedge class on bunker-mvp: CI transient-unit storm saturates logind D-Bus dispatch; single-arg busctl introspect probe is INVALID (false wedged reads)
reasoning: Verified live 21:00-21:07Z. 4th same-day wedge report (intervals 10.1h/4.7h/<25min). REAL finding A: bunker repo CI (actions.runner on bunker-mvp) churns thousands of transient units; NFailedUnits hit 2351; dbus-monitor showed UnitRemoved + NFailedUnits PropertiesChanged from systemd1 at high rate; strace on logind: 3709 epoll iterations in 12s draining fd 15 (systemd1 signal source) — logind is CPU/dispatch-saturated by the unit churn (user@<uid> and user-runtime-dir@<uid> failures from uid churn 1370-1390 dominate). Fixes applied: systemctl reset-failed (92->~7) + restart logind 21:05:27Z. CRITICAL CORRECTION B: the wedge PROBE itself was partly false: 'busctl introspect org.freedesktop.login1' without the object path is an invalid invocation (needs service + object); its nonzero rc reads as wedged. Proper probes: two-arg introspect, get-property NCurrentSessions (instant, t3), loginctl list-sessions. Post-fix: bunker_logind_up=1 in textfile + at fleet-monitor:9090; 0 spawn failures; alertmanager only cx53 TargetUnreachable x2. C: userdel SIGKILL class recurred at 21:03:34Z (bunker-0efd94ff): the new refusal path (commit 3498c527) WORKED AS DESIGNED — bunkerd surfaced the surviving home instead of claiming destroyed; manual userdel -r reclaimed home+user. RECOMMENDATION: (1) fix exporter/alert probe to two-arg busctl introspect or busctl get-property; (2) CI storm: NFailedUnits noise — scope transient unit churn in bunker CI tests or logind mask of Manager signal subscription is not possible; consider CI runner offload; (3) logind restart is symptomatic — the driver is CI unit churn, not a leak.

reasoning:
WHY (verified live this tick, 2026-10-18 04:2xZ): MON-GAP-025 (status complete) was filed to stop the benign recurring class from waking a triage pass every day. Live reality on fleet-monitor: `curl localhost:9093/api/v2/silences` -> [] (empty); deployed /root/fleet-monitoring/stack/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml holds exactly two inhibit_rules (HostDown -> warning/info; DiskFull -> DiskWillFillIn24h) and NO route for OOMKillsLowPressure or BunkerSpawnFailures; the lane workdir mirror monitoring/fleet-monitoring/stack/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml is byte-equivalent on this point (same two inhibits). MON-GAP-025's own foreman_note reads 'Worker dispatched but killed after 6min without c[ompleting]' — the row was closed with the deliverable absent. The class is still live: OOMKillsLowPressure{bunker-mvp} fired 2026-10-18T04:15:38Z (the current tick window) and dmesg on bunker-mvp confirms the benign shape (constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG, oom_memcg=/bunker-cgroup-test, task=python3 at 04:14:14Z) — exactly the row's own definition of noise.

TECHNICAL FINDING (why the row's preferred fix cannot ship as written): the suggested form 'inhibit OOMKillsLowPressure when oom_memcg matches a test memcg AND MemAvailable >= 15%' is NOT expressible. Alertmanager inhibit rules match on LABELS of other firing alerts; they cannot read metric series, and neither node_vmstat_oom_kill nor any rule annotation carries a memcg dimension. Checked this tick: the only per-container OOM series in the central Prometheus is cadvisor's container_oom_events_total (present for bunker-mvp, job=prometheus.scrape.cadvisor), but the CI victims live in an ephemeral cgroup /bunker-cgroup-test created by the Actions runner, not in a container — so a cadvisor-based scope filter would not see them. Same for 'BunkerSpawnFailures when bunker_logind_up == 1' (metric condition).

HONEST OPTION SET for the owner (pick one; each is one bounded change, all as-code, none done this tick):
 (a) ROUTE-TO-NULL: add a child route in stack/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml matching the two alertnames to a receiver that does NOT post to alert-router. The alert keeps firing and stays visible in Alertmanager/Grafana/Prometheus — only the board row stops. Effective for a flapping alert (repeat_interval does nothing here: each resolve->fire pair is a fresh notification). COST: a real low-pressure OOM on those hosts would no longer become a board row (the critical sibling OOMKillsOccurring, pressure >= threshold, still pages).
 (b) RULE-LEVEL SCOPE: only if a memcg/constraint dimension can be exported (node_exporter textfile from the hosts, or cgroup-aware scraping) — then scope the rule itself and keep full board delivery. Needs a producer, so it is a real work item, not a config edit.
 (c) SUPPRESS REPEATS AT THE ROUTER: alert-router already dedupes per alert+day; extending that to 'per stable fingerprint, suppress after N benign instances/day' trades a little signal loss for zero triage cost and touches this repo's own product (stack/alert-router/router.py) with the existing test battery as the gate.
WHAT: owner picks (a)/(b)/(c); then deploy via `docker compose up -d alertmanager` (a: validate first with `amtool check-config`), prove from outside (synthetic webhook re-fire must add NO new finding row, or /api/v2/silences shows the rule), and add the matching repo change so the repo and the host do not diverge again. NOTE: MON-GAP-025 should be reopened or superseded by this row — do not treat it as delivered.
ACCEPTANCE: a benign OOMKillsLowPressure/bunker-mvp re-fire (or a BunkerSpawnFailures re-fire) produces zero NEW pending finding rows on the monitoring board, while OOMKillsOccurring (critical, low MemAvailable) still produces a row; the mechanism is present in the published repo AND on the live host, and is reversible with one config commit.

title: MON-GAP-030 — the spool drain dedupes by row-id PRESENCE only, so an alert that re-fires after its row is closed is swallowed: DiskFull on bunker-mvp fired 4x on 2026-10-20 and landed nowhere
reasoning:
WHY: drain-board-rows.sh decides whether a spooled row is a duplicate by grepping the target board for the quoted row id and skipping on any hit. Row ids are MON-<LANE>-<FP8>-<YYYYMMDD> (alert fingerprint + UTC date), so the SECOND and later firings of the same condition on the same day reuse the first firing's id. The moment the first row is closed (status complete/done), every later firing of that same condition is silently swallowed and the live alert has no open work item — the alert-becomes-no-executed-work failure this lane exists to prevent. EVIDENCE (live, 2026-10-20): spool /tmp/fleet-monitoring-spool/board-rows.jsonl (732 lines, mtime 15:15Z) carries DiskFull-on-bunker-mvp firing rows at 13:03Z, 13:42Z, 14:07Z, 15:15Z each with a -RESOLVED twin; the board's row for that id was closed verification-only at 09:26Z; the 15:54Z drain reported appended=0 skipped=732 with zero unwritable rows; the alert was still firing at 15:58Z with bunker-mvp / at 100% (688M free). WITNESS: live:fleet-monitor:9090 + spool replay. The same shape hides repeats of every alert class whose first row of the day is closed — the drain cannot tell 'already handled and open' from 'handled, closed, and now firing again'.

FIX SHAPE (dispatched to a worker this tick): in drain-board-rows.sh, when a spooled FIRING row's id is present on the board, classify the board rows carrying that id — TERMINAL = complete/done/closed/verified-benign/duplicate/rejected/unverified-expired, anything else OPEN. Any OPEN row with that id keeps today's skip. If ALL rows for that id are TERMINAL, append ONE row (the newest firing row for that id in the batch, never the -RESOLVED twin) and print a refire line; never append more than one row per id per run, so a flapping alert adds at most one row per drain. The appended row is pending, so the next run dedupes it again — idempotency is preserved. Acceptance is a fixture test (monitoring/scripts/test-drain-refire.sh) over the drain's BOARD_ROOT/SPOOL/BOARD_APPEND/DRY overrides covering: re-fire appends exactly 1; second run appends 0; an OPEN row still dedupes; a new id still appends; a 4-row flap batch appends exactly 1; a lane with no board is still reported and appended 0.
